focus: This week's focus: joins, aggregation, and window functions. Try the prompts, then compare with the sample solutions.

challenges.title: Revenue by product
challenges.prompt: Using order_items, calculate total sales value for each product. Return product_id and revenue, highest revenue first.
challenges.starter:
SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS revenue
FROM order_items
GROUP BY product_id
ORDER BY revenue DESC;
challenges.solution: SELECT product_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS revenue FROM order_items GROUP BY product_id ORDER BY revenue DESC;
challenges.hint: Line value = quantity multiplied by unit_price; group by product_id.

challenges.title: Customers with no orders
challenges.prompt: List every customer who has never placed an order. Return customer_id and customer_name.
challenges.starter:
SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name
FROM customers c
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;
challenges.solution: SELECT c.customer_id, c.customer_name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL;
challenges.hint: A LEFT JOIN keeps every customer; unmatched order columns become NULL.

challenges.title: Rank employees by salary
challenges.prompt: Rank employees from highest to lowest salary within each department. Return employee name, department_id, salary and rank.
challenges.starter:
SELECT name, department_id, salary,
       DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank
FROM employees
ORDER BY department_id, salary_rank;
challenges.solution: SELECT name, department_id, salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank FROM employees ORDER BY department_id, salary_rank;
challenges.hint: Use DENSE_RANK() OVER with PARTITION BY department_id.
